The LanFEG proteins, which are found in this genus, consist of an ATP-binding domain and two transmembrane domains.Important genes in organisms of this genus includeska and emm. Based on the carbohydrate compositions of these organisms'cell walls, they are classiÂed as A-H, L, N, and R&S according to the LanceÂeld grouping. The CAMP test is used to identifyone organism in this genus, which can be transferred to neonates passing through the birth canal and inflames cow udders,rendering them unable to produce milk, explaining its species name agalactiae. This genus undergoes cell division along a singleaxis, and grows in pairs or chains, hence its name. Rheumatic fever is caused by the pyogenes species of these bacteria, whosepneumoniae species is, appropriately enough, the leading cause of bacterial pneumonia. White exudate covers the tonsils inthe pharyngitis caused by the group A bacteria of this kind. Name these spherical-shaped bacteria that can causea namesake sore throat.

Some members of this phylum contain a hook for gripping onto objects called a rostellum and anadhesive patch called a myzorhynchus. One member of this phylum reproduces by generating azygote that is surrounded by an oncosphere, which eventually becomes the hexacanth protectivecovering. The tegument that covers this phylum of animals is lined with folds called microtriches. Thisphylum's class Monogenea is distinguished by the presence of its haptors, while its class Cestoda isnoted for its proglottids. Although they are not rotifers, this phylum of animals osmoregulate by groupsof flame cells that are called protonephridia. This phylum of animals includes flukes and tapeworms. For10 points, name this phylum that mostly consists of flatworms.

One perturbative solution to this kind of problem takes the form of an infinite series of Feynmandiagrams that diverges. When finding an approximation for this kind of problem in the case of longwavelengths, the exponential term simply vanishes and all that must be integrated is the interactionpotential; that is a special case of the Born Approximation. In quantum mechanics, this kind ofproblem usually is solved by finding the associated amplitude of a wave, given that a plane waveencounters a potential and is transformed into a spherical wave. Classically, this type of problem istypically solved by finding the namesake angle given the impact parameter. Name thiskind of process in which a particle changes direction after a collision.

Diamminesilver(I) hydroxide can react with the simplest of compounds to produce a dianion usedin Reppe Chemistry. One type of cycloaddition occurs when these compounds react with alkenes andcarbon monoxide in the Pauson-Khand reaction. One type of compound containing this functionalgroup has a pKa of 25, and can be deprotonated using sodamide; that is its terminal variety.Reacting excess Br2 with these compounds yields geminal dihalides, while a poisoned palladium catalystis often used to prevent these compounds from completely hydrogenating to form alkanes. For 10points, name this class of organic compounds containing sp-hybridized carbons characterized by a triplebond, and whose simplest member is acetylene.

This organism's genome acquired a virulence factor from the 933W prophage. One product of thisorganism, which is named for a different bacterium, is a toxin whose A subunit cleaves the 28Sribosomal RNA and whose B subunit binds to globo-tri-aosyl-ceramide. Children infected by thisorganism can suffer from a form of kidney failure similar to TTP called hemolytic-uremic syndrome.Unusually for its species, it fails the Sereny invasion test, it cannot grow in 0.15% bile salts, and it doesnot ferment sorbitol. It's not Shigella, but this organism has the ability to produce shiga-like toxin.name this infectious gram-negative bacterium, which has the serotype O157:H7, istransmitted by undercooked hamburgers, and causes bloody diarrhea.

In particle physics, this word names peaks in the cross section of a scattering experimentcorresponding to the indirect observation of short-lived particles. The "width" within which this effectcan take place is equal to the viscous coefficient over the mass, and as that gamma ratio decreases,this effect becomes more pronounced. In LC circuits, this effect occurs alongside minimum impedanceat one over the square root of inductance times capacitance. The Q-factor can be defined as theratio of this effect's associated frequency to the aforementioned width. Via a von Karman vortex street,this effect destroyed the Tacoma Narrows bridge. Name this increase in amplitude thatoccurs when an oscillator is driven at its natural frequency.

One division within this period is marked by the appearance of Pseudostaffella antiqua. Containinginternal stages such as the Serpukhovian, Bashkirian and Gzhelian, it saw Laurasia and what wouldbecome China enclosing the Paleo-Tethys Sea. During it, the 6-foot long centipede Arthropleura andMeganeura, a dragonfly with a wingspan over 2 feet, thrived. Formation of the Urals began duringit. It saw the emergence of the amniote egg, which allowed eggs to be borne on land. This period wascharacterized by large rainforests, which later died to give this period its name. Name thisperiod divided into the Mississippian and Pennsylvanian, occurring from 359 to 299 million years ago,named for its coal-creating swamps.

Most of this scientist's work was summarized in a memorandum to Marcus Rhoades that diagrams a "repulsive force." Thisbiologist helped George Beadle's Stanford lab out of a quagmire by devising a way to visualize the seven pairs of Neurosporachromosomes. This scientist described how telomeres split off, replicate to form two sister chromatids without telomeres,which then fuse with one another, in the breakage-fusion-bridge cycle. Apart from ethnographic trips to South and CentralAmerica, this scientist entered a decade of relative silence in the 1950s aftfter publishing the results of experiments conducted atCold Spring Harbor Laboratory. This biologist found that activator factor was needed alongside the Ds locus in order to causea mutation in the Bz allele, in an experiment analyzing chromosome 9 of a triploid tissue. This 1983 Nobel winner devised thetheory of "controlling elements" based experiments she conducted on maize. Name this woman who discoveredjumping genes, or transposons.

The Weaire-Phelan structure is a solution to this scientist's namesake problem that seeks to Âfind an arrangement of cells ofequal volume that minimizes the surface area of their common walls. The theory of Ostwald ripening, an effect in which largemolecules in a solution grow at the expense of smaller ones, is based on an equation which states that vapor pressure at aninterface depends on the curvature of the interface, named for this scientist and Gibbs. A type of nondispersive oceanic wavethat balances Coriolis forces against either topographical boundaries or against another instance of the same wave is named after this scientist. This scientist is the first namesake of a phenomenon in which shear flow of a light flfluid on top of a heavierone generates instability at their interface. An inviscid flfluid will have constant vorticity around a closed loop according to atheorem formulated by this scientist. Identify this physicist who names an instability with Helmholtz, a "circulationtheorem," and an absolute temperature scale.

An octahedral chiral ruthenium complex known as a "molecular light switch" is non-luminescent in the presence of thiscompound. No fewer than 28 of these molecules are present in the transition metal complex misleadingly known as "zirconylchloride," and two of them are present in perrhenic acid. A bond in this molecule is ionized to allow metal ions to polymerizein the olation process. The stability region of this compound is the limiting factor often displayed in Pourbaix diagrams. Inmost complexes featuring them, six of these monodentate, reallyweak sigma-donating ligands coordinate to a transition metal,and the overall charge is 2+ or 3+. Highly charged transition metal complexes exchange these ligands for this compound insolution exponentially slower than mildly-charged complexes. At high pHs, these ligands transform into oxido ligands. Thepresence of this compound can be represented by writing the formula, then by adding a dot and indicating how many of thesemolecules there are; salts with formulas written thusly are called hydrates. Name this molecule which is the onlyligand in metal aqua complexes.

This material can have thin blade-shaped projections known as platelets in a layer known as the skeletal layer. This materialcan contain features called polynyas, which exist in sensible and latent heat varieties, with the latter being formed primarilythrough the action of katabatic winds. Formation of this material begins with frazil, which in calm conditions proceeds toform nilas, which then via raftfting produce the congelation form of this substance. The biosphere arising within and aroundthis substance is dominated by diatoms. Microwave imaging from satellites such as NASA's SMMR and the Defense Department'sSSM/I are used to track the seasonal extent of this substance, whose high albedo is instrumental in keeping theatmosphere cool. The movement of this substance south through the Fram Strait into the North Atlantic can disrupt thethermohaline circulation. Identify this substance which forms seasonally near the poles from liquid water.

A simple model of one form of this phenomenon shows that it is mostly a result of the difference of density of states at the Fermi level in spin subbands in both electrodes. That model has been superseded by Slonczewski's model and was Julliere's model. This phenomenon can be used to determine whether a Fermi surface is in contact with the Brillouin zone boundary. This phenomenon can generally be observed when the mean angle turned between collisions, or the cyclotron frequency times relaxation time, is greater than one. Kohler's rule is a scaling rule for this phenomenon. One form of it is caused by the RKKY interaction and was discovered in antiferromagnetically coupled multilayers of iron and chromium by Baibich, et al. That was its "giant" form, which is used in hard drives. Name this phenomenon, which includes the Hall effect, in which a material's resistivity changes with the application of a magnetic field.

McConnell's cannibalism experiments with members of this phylum contributed to the concept of "memory RNA". Members of this phylum are responsible for the grass-blade climbing behavior of Dictyoselium. One class contained in this phylum features a scolex and excretes waste via protonephridia. Several species in this phylum experience part of their life cycle in snails and cause Katayama fever. Like rotifers and nemerteans, these organisms excrete waste via flame cells. Members of this phylum possess auricles containing tactile cells and chemoreceptors and also have light-sensince ocelli. This phylum includes the organisms that cause schistosomiasis. These unsegmented, bilaterally symmetric organisms are acoelomates. Name this phylum, which contains classes such as Turbellaria and Trematoda and organisms like planarians.

Eggen, Lynden-Bell, and Sandage studied the velocities of 221 dwarf stars to formulate a theory about one instance of this process. The seeds for this process are the primordial overdensities reflected in the CMB fluctuations, which serve as nucleation points for this process. This process is the first step of hierarchical structure formation, and its products are cooled through a combination of Compton scattering, free-free emission, recombination, and collision-induced de-excitation. The halo masses for a given redshift for products of this process can be calculated via the Press-Schechter formalism. This process is believed to proceed via the spherical collapse model and results in the formation of the smallest objects capable of exceeding the Jeans criterion for virialization in the early universe. Identify this process, which results in the formation of the first gravity-bound structure in the universe, objects which come in dwarf, elliptical, and spiral varieties.

A method of spectroscopy for analyzing these molecules can be enhanced using reagents like PBN and DMPO. Two of these molecules are generated by treatment of an ether with butyl-lithium in the [1,2] Wittig rearrangement. Alkyl varieties of these molecules can adopt planar, rigid pyramidal, and flexible pyramidal structures. A common method for polymerizing styrene involving these molecules begins by heating benzoyl peroxide. When these reactions are depicted, they require the use of fishhook arrows, and reactions that involve these molecules are generally separated into three steps: initiation, propagation and termination. The disproportionation of one of them is catalyzed by superoxide dismutase. Name these molecules containing one or more unpaired electrons that are stabilized by antioxidants.

This statement can be used in electrodynamics to suggest that all plasmoids expand if not limitedby external forces. Special relativity modifies this statement into defining an interval rather than afixed value. For gravitational and electrostatic systems, this statement reduces to Lagrange's identity.This statement is derived by finding one-half of the time derivative of the moment of inertia, thentaking the time average of the time derivative of this value. A common assumption related to thistheorem is that systems are stably bound. With systems involving potential energy, it reduces to thestatement that the total average of 2K is equal to n times the total average of V. Name thismechanical theorem that relates the average kinetic and potential energies of a mechanical system.

Concentrations of these compounds are measured using either bipyradyl or phenanthroline in atitration. When using these substances, adding 1,2-dibromoethane as an activator creates bubbles ofethylene as the reaction progresses. Their central atom has a tetrahedral geometry with two solventmolecules filling the unbonded sites. These compounds are stored in either diethyl ether or THFdepending on which side of the Schlenk equilibrium you want them on. Two equivalents of thesecompounds are required to react with an ester, and they are most commonly used as carbonnucleophiles to attack carbonyl groups in order to create alcohols. Name theseorganomagnesium halides used to form carbon-carbon bonds, named for a French chemist.

Structures characteristic of these events lie nearby suture zones, and those terranes can besurrounded by nappes. Delamination is one process by which these events can occur, and theirnamesake cycle's final stages involve formation of batholiths and tectonic uplift. These events can bearranged into alpine, hercynotype, and cordilleran types, and these events can occur at mid-oceanridges or at subduction zones. The Caledonian one occured after the collision of fragments of the formerGondwana, and the Appalachian one was a result of the collision of North America and Africa. For 10points, name these geologic events that provide the primary mechanism for the formation ofmountains.

One receptor important in the metabolism of this substance contains a YTRF endocytotic signal. Themaster regulator of the metabolism of this substance is encoded by the HAMP gene. Duodenalcytochrome b reduces this substance in the gut, allowing it to be taken up by DMT1 transporters. Thissubstance binds to an RNA element containing a CAGUGN hairpin, which is called its namesakeresponse element. The cytoplasmic form of aconitase serves as a sensor of the levels of this element,because that protein contains a cluster of this element and sulfur. Hemochromatosis is an overloadof this substance. This metal is coordinated to histidine residues in an oxygen-carrying protein. It isstored in ferritin. Name this element which is coordinated to porphyrin of the hemeprosthetic group of hemoglobin.

Invitrogen's BLOCK-iT algorithm is used to design high-throughput screens using this process. Oneprotein used in this process was named for Arabidopsis mutants whose leaves looked like octopi. SID-1 encodes a channel necessary for this process in C. Elegans, which uses this process to regulate lin-14via lin-4 during development. The aforementioned protein, Argonaute, makes up the catalytic subunitof the RISC complex, which uses the small interfering molecules generated by DICER. This processresults in either inhibition of translation or degradation of the target messenger, leading to geneknockdown. Name this process whereby single-stranded RNA is silenced thanks to therecognition of double-stranded RNA with the same sequence.

This process cannot occur after intersystem crossing because it is spin-allowed, and the SternVolmerrelationship maps its disappearance. The distance between two molecules with this propertyis measured based on the inverse-sixth power dependence of this process's namesake resonanceenergy transfer to distance. Namethis form of luminescence contrasted with phosphorescence.

According to the Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem, one form of this property for a set of numbersimplies another form of this property for the corresponding powers of e. In mathematical logic,forcing is a technique which can be used to prove results regarding consistency and this property. Fora sequence of random variables, this property suffices, but is not necessary, to show that the sum oftheir variances is equal to the variance of their sum. In probability, two events have this property ifthe probability of their intersection is equal to the product of their probabilities. The elements of a basisfor a vector space have this property. Name this property, the linear form of which says noelement can be written as a linear combination of the others.

An equation named for this man predicts that electrons in free space will rapidly oscillate around amedian, called zitterbewegung. Along with Kapitsa, this man names an effect in which a particle beamis diffracted by a standing wave of light. Those objects, whose existence he showed to imply the quantization of electric charge and magnetic charge, are magnetic monopoles. He also theorized the existence ofpositrons based on his namesake relativistic wave equation for spin Â½ particles. Name thisEnglish physicist, the namesake of a generalized function which is 0 everywhere except at 0, and hasintegral one, his namesake delta function.

The undulation associated with this construct can be obtained by solving the Bruns equation, and experimental measurements of this construct have been assisted by measurements from the the recent GRACE satellite mission. Anomalies in this construct are typically analyzed by subtracting the second zonal harmonic coefficient, and one approximate method of creating this construct is evaluating the gravimetric Stokes integral. The influence of surface features on this construct is minimized due to isostacy and this construct's intermediate-scale highs are associated with subduction zones. This construct is formed by neglecting tidal forces and constructing an equipotential surface based on interior density variations. Identify this theoretical construct which represents the mean sea level that would obtain if the earth were covered in water

Septins, which exert antibacterial activity against Shigella species, are a relatively reecntly discovered component of this system. Experiments conducted on Listeria, which co-opts this structure in its hosts using its protein ActA, suggest that the elastic propulsion mechanism is the primary means by which this structure exerts force. The narrowest components of this structure are assembled with the aid of ABPs like fimbrin and filamin, the latter of which imparts three-dimensional structure. Another component of this structure is assembled in its namesake organizing center in structures like basal bodies, and is a tubulin polymer to which motor proteins can attach. Name this intracellular structure composed of three types of fibers, which gives the cell its shape.

A reagent whose commercial name contains the word Alpine and this moiety's name is used in a stereoselective reduction of carbonyls to alcohols called the Midland reduction. The reaction of a catechol derivative containing this moiety with an alkyne and subsequent treatment with bromine yields a trans vinyl compound with this moiety. Compounds with this moiety, such as 9-BBN, may be coupled with organohalides under base and palladium catalysis to yield hydrocarbons in a reaction named for Suzuki. Cis-hydration of olefins may be achieved by synthesis of a trialkyl compound centered on this moiety, followed by treatment with sodium hydroxide and hydrogen peroxide. Application of a sodium salt containing this moiety, which is a weaker analog of lithium aluminum hydride, is the simplest method of adding this functional group to a compound. Name this functional group which is electron-deficient and whose dimeric form contains a 3-center 2-electron bond.

MOPAs use these devices in serial with an amplifier to measure their gain. The addition of an etalon with the appropriate finesse parameter to one of these devices can be used to convert multimodal output into unimodal output. The exciplex variant of this device operates by triggering the formation and subsequent separation of unstable noble gas-halide complexes. Resonance trapping can increase the upper level lifetime in these devices by channeling the output from transitions to the ground state back into the device's medium. Pulsed output in these devices may be accomplished by Q-switching, in which the cavity is periodically obstructed to prevent resonance. These devices operate by pumping from a ground state to a metastable state, from which a cascade is induced, a technique known as population inversion. Name these devices that emit coherent light by means of stimulated emission.

According to the Oort equation, one form of this quantity relative to the LSR is equal to omega minus omega nought times R nought times the sin of the angle between the object and the observer. The mass of a spiral galaxy is equal to the galaxy's radius times this quantity squared over big G. For an elliptical galaxy, the galaxy's effective radius, luminosity, and the range of this quantity are related by the fundamental plane. According to the Tulley-Fischer relationship, a spiral galaxy's luminosity is roughly related to the fourth power of this quantity. The "peculiar" form of this quantity is not accounted for by Hubble's Law. The force caused by a magnetic field is equal to a particle's charge multiplied by this quantity crossed with the field strength. The square root of 2GM over radius is equal to the escape form of this quantity for a spherical body. This quantity squared over radius is equal to centripetal acceleration. Name this quantity that is equal to distance over time.

Colorimetric analysis using DCIP is used to quantitatively measure the action of this complex in the Hill reaction. One section of this complex oscillates through four different S states whose efficiency is characterized by the Kok parameters. Another section of this complex contains D1 and D2 subunits, each of which contains a pheophytin cofactor. It contains P680, which ejects an electron and passes it onto plastoquinone; that electron was moved by resonance effects from the LHC. This complex contains the oxygen-evolving complex, which takes two water molecules and produces 4 electrons and one O2 molecule as a byproduct. Name this protein complex in the thylakoids, the first one involved in the light reactions of photosynthesis.

For a function with this property on a disk that is non-negative over that disk, an upper and lower bound is provided by Harnack's Inequality. They're not entire or analytic functions, but any function that has this property over the entire plane and is bounded above or below must be constant according to Liouville's Theorem. The Poisson Integral Formula produces a continuous function with this property on a disk given fixed values for the function on the boundary, which is the objective of the Dirichlet Problem. The real and imaginary parts of an analytic function both have this property and are called "conjugates." The divergence of the gradient of these functions is equal to 0. Name these functions, which satisfy Laplace's Equation, and which are described by the same adjective as the series defined as the sum from n = 1 to infinity of one over n.

This technique is widely used for label-free visualization of lipidic cellular structures in an eponymous "coherent" type of microscopy. The formation of a charge-transfer complex between analyte molecules and silver nanoparticles is one mechanism of signal enhancement in a surface-enhanced version of this technique. The intensity of the signal of this technique is proportional to the square of the electric dipole moment, or the polarizability times the electric field. Performing this technique requires "notch filters" to cut off signals from Rayleigh scattering. The signals from this technique represent either a loss or gain of energy after an inelastic collision with a photon. It is most useful for analyzing symmetrical vibrations of nonpolar groups, unlike IR spectroscopy. Name this technique that produces "Stokes" and "anti-Stokes" frequencies and which measures the shape of a molecule using a type of scattering named for an Indian physicist.

The decay of this particle into a pion and a neutrino-antineutrino pair provides a chance tomeasure rho and eta, two parameters in the Wolfenstein parametrization of the CKM matrix. Dalitzfirst applied his namesake technique to the decay of these particles. In 1999, Fermilab's KTeV teamfound that the value for a double ratio of different modes of decay of these particles and theirantiparticles was 28 plus or minus 4.1 all times 10 to the minus 4. That double ratio is epsilon primeover epsilon. Providing evidence that the long-lived neutral type of this particle decayed into twopions won Cronin and Fitch a Nobel Prize. Name this particle in which CP violation wasdiscovered and which was the cause of the tau-theta puzzle.

A visual representation of this entity's three hour Kp index is Bartels musical diagram. TheSvalgaard-Mansurov effect is an asymmetry that occurs due to a negative y component of an entitythat interacts with this region. Stormer theory deals with the existence of forbidden regions in thisentity, based on a cut-off rigidity. This region is associated with the Chapman-Ferraro cavity, and Birkeland currents descend from this region to the ionosphere and then back up again. The inner radiationbelt in this region is also called the van Allen belt. At the boundary of this region is the bow shock. For 10points, name this tear shaped region surround the Earth that is formed when the solar wind and itsinterplanetary magnetic field interacts with the Earth's magnetic field.

Burg and Burg found that the ability of compounds to elicit the same responses as this planthormone had a direct correlation with their ability to accept pi orbital electrons. Precursors to thiscompound are formed through the MSAE pathway, in which methionine is used to generate AdoMet,or SAM, in the Yang cycle. Conversion of AdoMet into the immediate precursor to this compound ismediated by a pyridoxal enzyme that is inhibited by AVG. That immediate precursor is ACC. Neljubov was the first to discover that this compound's presence in illuminating gas caused plants to growhorizontally. Along with horizontal growth, elongation inhibition and swelling are part of the "tripleresponse" to this plant hormone. Name this gaseous hydrocarbon and plant hormone thatripens fruit.

The propagation of these objects through the heliosphere is typically modeled using a radial diffusion coefficient that depends on the spiral angle of the interplanetary field to the sun's radius vector. An anomalous variant of these objects appears to have been discovered by the AGASA experiment, and spallation reactions with these objects are thought to be responsible for light-element nucleosynthesis. At energies above 10 to the 19 electron-volts, these particles begin to scatter against CMB photons; this fact, manifested as the so-called "knee" in their energy spectrum, places an upper limit on the energies of these particles from extragalactic sources, known as the GZK cutoff. The activity of these particles undergoes an 11-year cycle modulated by solar activity. Primarily composed of protons and other charged nuclei, identify these energetic particles from space.

The scientist who worked out the theory behind this device outlined a "passivity criterion" which held if the charge-dependent proportionality function was strictly positive. The dynamics of these devices correlate with the dynamics of neural synapses, suggesting neuromorphic applications, and at the nanoscale, these devices exhibit pinched hysteresis loops. The original realization of this device employed two platinum contacts sandwiching a junction between doped and undoped titanium oxide. This device's inventor hypothesized that there should exist a device that related charge to the flux; thus, this device maintains a constant resistance until it is overdriven, at which point the resistance changes, allowing this device to be used as a Boolean logic element. Identify this basic circuit element invented by Leon Chua, which can be used as a non-volatile memory cell.

In side forms of this signaling pathway, a complex with Daam1 is formed, which eventually leads to the activation of ROCK. The receptors for one form of this signaling pathway bind to LRP and may also bind to other factors such as axin. The main signaling molecule in this pathway is found in high concentrations in Spemann's Organizer. The main effect of this pathway is to affect DNA-binding transcription factors called LEF/TCF. Those receptors for this pathway are GPCRs that form part of the frizzled family. Downstream of the receptor, GSK3 is turned off, which leads to the buildup of beta-catenin, which eventually migrates into the nucleus. Name this signaling pathway whose name derives from the wingless gene of the fruit fly and which modulates neural induction, differentiation, and neural crest differentiation.

Karpf and Trussaudi developed a modified reaction that avoids the customary use of one of these compounds to open an epoxide in the conventional synthesis from shikimic acid of oseltamivir. Carolyn Bertozzi discovered a bioorthogonal reaction that reacts these compounds with certain phosphines to yield an amide linkage, useful in the labelling of cell surfaces. A similar reaction combines these compounds with phosphines to yield primary amines, known as the Staudinger reaction. Acyl versions of these compounds can undergo the Curtius rearrangement to form isocyanates. Inorganic salts of these compounds are often used in airbags due to the fact that they readily decompose into nitrogen gas., name these compounds that contain three nitrogens bound to each other.

The tumor-suppressing gene GRAF1 has been shown to control one pathway of this process, in which CLICs organize molecules into GEECs. That pathway, along with one that uses IL2 receptors, requires the GTPase dynamin. Lsm1 and Pil1 participate in a form of this process that occurs at eisosomes, and in adipocytes and endothelial cells this process often occurs at caveolae. The most studied variant of this process is mediated by a protein that organizes itself into a triskelion and drives the formation of coated pits; that protein is called clathrin. One example of a molecule upon which this process acts is transferin, and endosomes are formed in this process. Name this process by which cells take in molecules that cannot pass through the cell membrane.

In a funeral eulogy, this man claimed that one of his rivals mingled fanciful conceptions withscience and left behind laboriously constructed, vast edifices on imaginary foundations. Based onlyon a drawing by Cosimo Collini, this scientist identified a pterosaur as a flying reptile and named it a"ptero-dactyle". One of his most important books was Research on the Fossil Bones of Quadrupeds.This scientist stated that if an animal's teeth were adapted for a certain type of food, then so must itsdigestive system, which was one of the bases for his "Principle of Correlation of Parts". This man'sefforts led to extinction being accepted as a scientific theory. He founded the field of vertebratepaleontology and pioneered the use of the comparative method. Name this biologist andgeologist best known for his advocation of catastrophism and opposition to Lamarck.

The Mermin-Wagner theorem proved that these processes could not occur in the two dimensionalXY model, but a form of this process does occur and is named for Kosterlitz and Thouless. A simplemodel for these processes in rod-like polymers was introduced by Onsager. One phenomenologicaltheory of these processes expands the free energy in a power expansion as a function of a smallamplitude order paramater. In liquid crystals, this process can occur between smectic A and nematic.These processes were classified based on the continuity of their derivative with respect to temperature byEhrenfest. Name this process in which a system is transformed to a different state of matter.

An important consideration when designing a circuit with this device is its setup and hold time.One circuit that makes use of XOR gates and these devices generates a periodic pseudo-randomsequence and is an LFSR. A modification of one type of this device has inputs from two AND gateswhich have an 'Enable' input in common; that type of this device is a pair of cross-coupled NORgates. Another one of these devices transitions to high or low according to the equation J AND KNOT, while the output of yet another type of this device is equal to its input. Name theseelectronic devices that offer a primitive form of memory and which include the D one and the SR latch.

An S-curve like hysteresis relation between temperature and surface density is the basis for thelimit cycle model of these objects. That model was first introduced to explain these objects in a subsetof cataclysmic variables also known as U Geminorum stars. Balbus and Hawley showed that theonset of turbulence in these objects could be caused by the magnetorotational instability. Amagnetized one of these was first proposed by Lynden-Bell and is the subject of theBlandford-Znajek process. Most models of them are based on the Shakura-Sunyaevalpha-prescription for anomalous stress. One of these is thought to surround a supermassive blackhole in quasars, and they can result from objects straying inside the Roche limit. Name thisstructure formed by debris in motion around a celestial body.

Phil Green created the Phred/Phrap/Consed package to assist in utilizing the results of thisprocess. Paul Hebert developed a taxonomic system that uses this technique on regions like CO1 andis called barcoding. When using the 454 GS-20, one step in this process involves emulsifying amixture in an oil suspension. A common approach to this process uses chain-terminating inhibitorsin the form of dideoxy bases and is named after Sanger. J. Craig Venter, as the president of CeleraCorporation, used a type of the shotgun method to perform this process. Name this processwhich determines the order of nucleotides in the blueprint of life.

A revolution in the solvent extraction of this element occurred as a result of the discovery of thereagent 5 nonyl salicylaldoxime. Jahn-Teller distortions are most widely studied and documented incomplexes of the +2 oxidation state of this element.
